title: Consumer commands are judged by the acting participant's `@mandate` profile; `ia position` stays ungated
summary: Breaking: @inventarch/cli now judges `ia read` and `ia next` (move Observation), `ia validate` and `ia preview` (Verification), `ia author` (Synthesis), and `ia capture`, its `ia compile` alias, `ia project` and a workspace `ia host <host> --apply`, which writes the same projection (Execution), by the acting participant's mandate profile (runtime governingMandates, defaultActor and profileRefusal) before they read or write anything; a capture or project plan is judged as the effect it plans, while a host plan, `ia host --remove` (which restores editing) and `ia host claude --user` are not judged. Where 2.0.0 ran these commands unconditionally, a workspace whose authored mandates do not grant the move, that names several participants and no `composition.steward`, or that holds a governing mandate the runtime cannot read (such as `authority.moves []`, which admission accepts) now refuses them at exit 1: IA-RUNTIME-MANDATE-MOVE, -WORD (preview and author only, for the word they write), -ACTOR, or IA-RUNTIME-REQUEST-INVALID. A workspace `ia init` creates grants all five moves to its one participant, so its commands run as before, and a workspace with no governing mandate restricts nothing. `ia position` and every command outside those modes are not gated, so the governance position every refusal names always runs. Each gated command accepts --actor <agent> (a canonical identity, `@agent <name>` or a bare name), which must be an authored participant of the repository's `@workspace`: an authored `@agent` a mandate scoped to it names, or its `composition.steward` when that is an authored `@agent`; an installed steward is no default actor. Naming an actor is a local declaration, not authentication: it resolves an open choice, and then that participant's own mandates are judged, which may be looser or stricter than the default actor's; it never lifts a move or excluded word those mandates state. Every refusal names one command that runs for the same actor in the same state: the governance position of the mandate concerned; under an open choice, or for a default actor no governing mandate binds, the same command with --actor naming the first participant whose mandates allow it; for an --actor that names no participant, the same command without it where the default actor may run it. Once a command's profile allows it, a refusal it raises later is held to the same rule: a next command of a gated mode the profile refuses becomes the governance position, and one it allows carries the named --actor. The machine routes, every `ia scope` form, MACHINE_PROTOCOL versions 1 and 2 and the runtime's own refusals are unchanged. Limits: actor selection is not host authentication; the edit guard re-keyed to `@mandate` is separate work.
